note: Recurrence of c.1069G>A in 11 of 14 discovery cohort patients with Kelch-domain clustering is well-documented, making evaluation of a CpG mutational hotspot versus ascertainment bias biologically sound and worth investigating.

evidence.text: In the discovery cohort of 14 individuals with de novo missense variants in KLHL20, 11 harbored the exact recurrent variant c.1069G>A (p.Gly357Arg), with all identified missense variants clustering in the Kelch-type beta-propeller domain.

source.title: De novo missense variants in the E3 ubiquitin ligase adaptor ...
source.quote: We observed a recurrent de novo missense variant in 11 patients (NM_014458.4:c.1069G>A p.[Gly357Arg]). The recurrent missense and the 3 other missense variants all clustered in the Kelch-type beta-propeller domain of the KLHL20 protein, which shapes the substrate binding surface.
